stories.title: Suspect should not be deprived of bail in case of 'reasonable doubt' over involvement, SC rules
summary: ISLAMABAD: Taking exception to the prosecution’s shifting stance without realising the gravity of that conduct in a case regarding expired drugs, the Supreme Court has ruled that whenever reasonable doubt arises, a suspect should not be deprived of the benefit of bail.

Based on these sections, a two-judge SC bench on April 16 granted post-arrest bail to the petitioner on furnishing bail bonds to the tune of Rs100,000 with two sureties in the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial court.

When the SC’s bail order was sent for compliance, it emerged that the prosecution modified the first information report (FIR) by replacing the original provisions with Sections 409, 471, 468, 467, 420, 109 of PPC, read with Section 5 (2) of the 1947 Prevention of Corruption Act.

stories.title: Apple will have limited iPhone Duo units available in stores on Friday
summary: Apple on Wednesday said it will have ‘limited’ numbers of its folding iPhone Duo phone available for walk-in customers when the device launches on Friday, after initial online orders sold out in minutes and pushed delivery times for some customers to January.

Other regions will only have iPhone Duo units available for customers who already bought them online, including mainland China, France, Hong Kong, India, Japan, Malaysia, South Korea, Taiwan, Thailand and the UAE, Apple said.
On the China-governed island of Macau, the iPhone Duo will be available for walk-in customers only, with limited inventory, Apple said.

stories.title: PM Shehbaz vows to strengthen Maldives ties for 'all time to come'; 20 MoUs signed
summary: Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Wednesday vowed to strengthen bilateral relations with the Maldives, as the two countries signed 20 memorandums of understanding (MoUs) during the visit of President Dr Mohamed Muizzu.
Concluding his remarks, PM Shehbaz said Muizzu’s visit had given Pakistan-Maldives relations “new purpose and new momentum”.
Muizzu, speaking to Dar, “expressed Maldives’ desire to deepen its close relations with Pakistan and explore new avenues of mutually beneficial cooperation”, FO said.

stories.title: Pakistani who allegedly defrauded US Postal Service remanded in NCCIA Lahore's custody
summary: LAHORE: A judicial magistrate on Wednesday granted the National Cyber Crime Investigation Agency (NCCIA) five-day physical remand of a suspect in an alleged Rs35 billion fraud involving the online sale of counterfeit US postage labels.

The NCCIA’s Lahore zone announced his arrest at a press conference a day ago, saying that the suspect operated a website to market and sell over 5m fake postage stamps over a period of more than three years.
The agency’s investigating officer told the court that the suspect had allegedly been operating a website, LabelsBank.com, since August 2023 to sell more than 5m counterfeit postage labels.

stories.title: OpenAI expands ChatGPT ads to 26 more countries, including Pakistan, in bid to boost revenue
summary: OpenAI said on Wednesday it was expanding advertising on ChatGPT to 26 more countries, including Pakistan, ​bringing the total to 89 as ‌the AI company beefs up its advertising business to boost revenue ahead of a potential initial public ​offering.
OpenAI began testing ads in ChatGPT ​in the US earlier this year, and ​more than 100,000 advertisers have since run campaigns on the platform, the company said.
Advertisers can access ​ChatGPT ads ​in the ⁠new markets through technology partners, or get self-service access via Ads Manager ​on the company’s platform.

stories.title: ATC appoints state counsel for Imaan, Hadi in security breach case
summary: ISLAMABAD: An anti-terrorism court on Wednesday appointed a state counsel to cross-examine prosecution witnesses from the defence side in a security breach case against lawyers Imaan Zainab Hazir-Mazari and Hadi Ali Chattha.

He had shown up in the Islamabad district and sessions court during a November hearing instead of Advocate Shakeel Jatt, the state counsel who was initially appointed to represent the duo in the case.

Imaan and Hadi’s rearrest The lawyer couple has been in jail since their arrest on Jan 23 in a case registered against them for protesting outside the Islamabad High Court and allegedly manhandling the IHC Bar Association president.

stories.title: JI announces third wave of anti-levy protests across country on Friday
summary: LAHORE: The Jamaat-i-Islami Pakistan (JI) announced on Wednesday that it will launch the third phase of its nationwide protest movement against the petroleum levy on Friday, with sit-ins planned in all districts across the country, according to a press release by the party.

Wednesday’s press release by JI said the new phase of demonstrations would begin on the instructions of party chief Hafiz Naeemur Rehman, and that the party’s clear and firm demand remained the complete abolition of the petroleum levy.
On Sept 20, the party launched a protest march towards Islamabad, warning that if the government failed to abolish the petroleum levy, the protest could turn into one to oust the government.

stories.title: Monitoring the monitors: US states prepare for surge of Justice Dept election watchers
summary: Some state and local laws allow election officials to prevent DOJ monitors from being present inside polling locations.
DOJ staff can observe voting, speak to voters after they leave polling places and report immediate concerns to local law enforcement or election officials.
Two Minnesota counties, Hennepin and Ramsey, invoked state law to keep DOJ monitors from within 30 metres of polling places during the primary election in August.

stories.title: ‘Where are the courts?’: Killing of Multan suspect in alleged CCD encounter sparks concern among lawyers, journalists
summary: The death of a suspect, allegedly during an exchange of fire with Punjab’s Crime Control Department (CCD), sparked questions from lawyers and journalists on Wednesday regarding extrajudicial killings and due process.
The Human Rights Commission of Pakistan (HRCP) alleged earlier this year that the CCD has adopted a “deliberate policy of staged police encounters leading to extrajudicial killings”.

Journalist Maryam Nawaz Khan termed it a “total failure of the system”. “When the state relies solely on CCD or police encounters, it’s an admission that our judicial system is dead,” she contended while commenting on Butt’s post.

stories.title: Pakistan, Qatar, Turkiye and Indonesia sign 'Badr' defence cooperation pact
summary: Pakistan, Qatar, Turkiye and Indonesia on Wednesday signed a multilateral pact to promote cooperation in defence production and capabilities, the Turkish defence ministry said.
Defence Minister Khawaja Asif, who was visible in pictures shared by the ministry, signed on behalf of Pakistan.

During his November 2025 visit to the Gulf state, President Asif Ali Zardari met with Qatari Emir Sheikh Tamim bin Hamad Al Thani and offered to expand bilateral cooperation in the areas of defence production.

stories.title: Pakistan's mythologised idea of an all-rounder finds a home in Arafat Minhas
summary: Arafat makes it look innate, even though it is anything but.
What was particularly remarkable about Arafat during the game was that he managed to take Pakistan out of situations that normally result in the team sinking further down.

Pakistan had a disappointing show last time out in India, but what was particularly disappointing was how the team’s spin arsenal fared even in favourable conditions — a dire set of sporting circumstances that culminated in the team’s first ever ODI loss to Afghanistan.

stories.title: Macron takes aim at Trump for using France riots for election gain
summary: President Emmanuel Macron on Wednesday took an apparent swipe at counterpart Donald Trump of exploiting France’s riots for advantage in the US midterm election battle, as Paris prepared for more protests this weekend.
France’s government has admitted it “lost control” in the frenzy of street violence that erupted last weekend, when masked youths clashed with police, looted shops and vandalised public buildings.
Since the rioting — the worst France has seen in years — and ahead of further cost-of-living demonstrations this coming Saturday, Macron’s government has warned it will brook no further violence.

stories.title: Nigeria confirms its first Ebola case is Bundibugyo strain
summary: The first Ebola case detected in Nigeria is the Bundibugyo strain, which is behind a major DR Congo outbreak, and the patient is a diplomat, an emergency meeting heard on Wednesday.

The case in Nigeria, Africa’s most populous country, was detected in a woman who had travelled from Uganda to the capital Abuja on Oct 3, the Nigeria Centre for Disease Control and Prevention (NCDC) said.

The World Health Organisation (WHO) also confirmed that it was the Bundibugyo strain, for which there is still neither a vaccine nor a specific treatment. “This person is actually a diplomat,” another official said, adding the patient has deteriorated into “multi-organ failure”.

stories.title: 10 killed, 44 injured as passenger bus overturns on highway in Punjab's Rajanpur
summary: DERA GHAZI KHAN: Ten people were killed and 44 others injured when a passenger bus overturned after hitting a road divider on the Indus Highway in Rajanpur district’s Rojhan tehsil, Rescue 1122 said.

Of the 44 wounded, 38 were being treated at the Rajanpur District Headquarters (DHQ) Hospital, while four critically injured persons were referred to Dera Ghazi Khan and two seriously hurt to Rahim Yar Khan’s Sheikh Zayed Hospital.
Rescue 1122 said it “responded promptly” upon receiving the emergency call and mobilised 10 ambulances and two rescue vehicles from Rajanpur, Jampur and Rojhan.

stories.title: US envoy to meet Putin after 'positive' talks with Zelensky
summary: Washington’s envoy Steve Witkoff arrived in Saint Petersburg early Wednesday to meet with Russian President Vladimir Putin following what US Secretary of State Marco Rubio described as “positive” talks with President Volodymyr Zelensky of Ukraine.
After talks with Witkoff in Oslo, Zelensky thanked Washington on Tuesday for the resumption of US intelligence sharing on Russian strikes.
Trump has also been keeping up the pressure on Ukraine, saying at the White House that he wanted Zelensky to “make a deal” with Russia, which is ramping up its strikes as a bitter winter looms.

stories.title: Tesla-SpaceX deal: Wall St says inevitable but Musk says it's not certain
summary: Elon Musk sees "a lot of merit" in combining Tesla and SpaceX, but the decision is ​not his to make: two special committees he cannot join and a Tesla shareholder vote he calls a high hurdle ‌stand in the way.
Tesla's vote is the hurdle Control may also be part of Musk's appeal for a merger.
Musk holds about 85% of SpaceX's voting power through super-voting shares. ‌But ⁠at Tesla he has roughly 20%.

stories.title: ECP orders fresh schedule for Islamabad local government polls
summary: ISLAMABAD: The Election Commission of Pakistan (ECP) on Wednesday directed its office to prepare and issue the election programme for local government elections in the Islamabad Capital Territory (ICT).

The Election Commission of Pakistan (ECP) on Wednesday ruled that Islamabad local government (LG) elections would be conducted under the ICT Local Government Act, 2015, adding that it would issue a schedule for the polls later in the day.

Raja further told the hearing that the interior minister, interior secretary and the chief commissioner, on behalf of the ministerial committee, had provided an undertaking. “It appears that the government does not wish to hold local government elections in Islamabad,” he said.

stories.title: Trump says companies should pay 'dividend' to communities to make data centres popular
summary: US President Donald Trump said on Wednesday that companies ​building data centres should pay a "dividend" to the communities ‌where they are sited if they want to make the developments popular.

"I have watched the process closely, and data centres that were highly unpopular in ​a certain area have become extremely popular when a ​financial deal is struck," Trump said in a Truth Social ⁠post.
Trump said in February that major technology companies must build their own power plants for their data centres in ​order to protect ​consumers from rising ⁠bills.

stories.title: Russia says it will send first diesel cargo to US on Thursday
summary: Russia will dispatch its first tanker with diesel for the United States on Thursday, Deputy Prime Minister Alexander Novak said, according to the Vedomosti news outlet, after a deal with US President Donald Trump.

Russia lifted its self-imposed ban on diesel exports on October 9, introduced to tackle domestic shortages triggered by Ukrainian drone attacks on refineries, after reaching the deal with Trump to supply diesel to global markets.
Russian President Vladimir Putin was hosting US special envoy Steve Witkoff on Wednesday, after the US-Russia diesel export deal led to a sharp deterioration in ties between the US and Ukraine.

stories.title: Jamal Said wins Pakistan Backyard ultra title for third time
summary: Pakistan’s renowned ultra-runner Jamal Said has won the Pakistan Backyard Ultra National Championship for the third time, completing 29 consecutive loops over 29 hours and covering a total distance of 194 kilometres.
The same year, he covered approximately 335 kilometres by completing 50 loops in a backyard ultra event.
Syed has now qualified for the Backyard Ultra World Championship for the third time.

stories.title: Pakistan sweep Bahrain in Billie Jean King Cup
summary: Ushna Suhail and Mahin Aftab Qureshi secured commanding singles victories before teaming up to complete the clean sweep in the Group A tie at the Pakistan Tennis Federation Tennis Complex.
The pair then joined forces in the doubles, defeating Eman Alzaimoor and Zaidan 6-1, 6-0 to seal Pakistan’s opening-day win.
Qatar claimed the doubles, with Hinda Al Mudahka and Khadija Gassama defeating Abualhaj and Sayej 6-3, 6-4.

stories.title: Profit rates on National Savings schemes increased from Oct 21
summary: ISLAMABAD: The government has increased profit rates on several national savings schemes, including those for pensioners, senior citizens and families of martyrs, with the revised rates taking effect from October 21.

According to the revised schedule issued by the Central Directorate of National Savings (CDNS), the profit rate on Behbood Savings Certificates, Pensioners’ Benefit Accounts and Shuhada’s Family Welfare Accounts has been raised to 12.96 per cent from 12.72pc.
The profit rate on Special Savings Certificates has been increased to 12pc from 11.6pc for the first five profit payments.

stories.title: French government faces fresh test as Yellow Vests mobilise
summary: France's Yellow Vest movement filed plans for a major ​march through Paris on Saturday, presenting the government with its next major test after riots and looting last weekend shook confidence ‌in its ability to maintain order.

Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu was due to meet union leaders on Wednesday, seeking ways to defuse one of the worst crises France has faced in recent years and avoid a repeat of the violence that swept French cities on October 17.

Read: French PM calls for 'partial curfews' in cities hit by riots and looting Government ministers have promised a vastly reinforced security operation after acknowledging shortcomings in their initial response, ​with troops expected to be deployed alongside additional police.

stories.title: England, Sri Lanka seek revival
summary: England will be desperate to get their campaign back on track when they face Sri Lanka in the second match of the ODI tri-series at the Rawalpindi Cricket Stadium on Thursday.
Harry Brook-led England, who recently defeated Sri Lanka in an ODI series at the latter's backyard, will need to address several weaknesses exposed in Tuesday's 87-run defeat by Pakistan.

England will hope that their first outing in Pakistan has provided valuable lessons and that greater familiarity with the conditions will help them produce a more disciplined performance against Sri Lanka.

stories.title: Turkiye plans mandate to send military personnel to Saudi Arabia, ruling party official says
summary: Turkiye will submit to parliament ​a mandate allowing for military personnel to be ‌deployed to Saudi Arabia under its joint defence pact with Saudi Arabia and Pakistan, a lawmaker from the ruling AK Party ​told Reuters on Wednesday.
A day earlier, Reuters reported that Turkiye submitted a defence ‌pact with Pakistan and Saudi Arabia to parliament for ratification, according to three parliamentary sources.

Turkiye, which has a robust defence industry, has condemned Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia, expressed willingness to help meet Riyadh's military technology needs and agreed to join ‌a Saudi-led ⁠coalition to ensure navigational safety in the Red Sea.

stories.title: 'Apartheid automation': How Israel uses AI to monitor Palestinian land, movement and lives
summary: In the occupied West Bank, AI-powered systems are helping Israeli authorities monitor land, buildings and movement, raising fears that the technology could facilitate demolitions and accelerate displacement.

From surveillance to military targeting Along with the system documented in the occupied West Bank primarily that involve monitoring and surveillance, investigations into Israel's operations in Gaza have raised separate concerns about AI-assisted military targeting.

Microsoft came under scrutiny in 2025 after The Guardian reported that an Israeli military intelligence unit used its Azure cloud platform to store recordings of Palestinian phone calls collected through surveillance in Gaza and the West Bank.

stories.title: Fact check: Viral video does not show Palestinian flag atop Eiffel Tower amid France riots; is AI generated
summary: Several people, including right-wing American accounts, have been sharing a video on social media platform X since October 19, claiming it shows a Palestinian flag hoisted at the top of the Eiffel Tower during protests in Paris.

How it started On October 19, an X account shared a video of flags being hoisted atop the Eiffel Tower, with the following caption: “Congratulations, Emmanuel Macron, you destroyed Paris.” The post gained 5.8 million views.
Fact-check status: false The claim that a viral video shows a Palestinian flag hoisted at the top of the Eiffel Tower in Paris is false.

stories.title: 10 killed, 35 injured as bus overturns on Rajanpur's Indus Highway
summary: At least 10 passengers were killed and 35 injured on Wednesday when a passenger bus travelling from Karachi to Dera Ghazi Khan overturned after hitting a divider on an under-construction road near Bangla Hidayat on the Indus Highway in Rajanpur, Rescue 1122 said.
In a separate accident reported the same day, four people, including women and children, were killed when a Mazda truck collided with an Alto car near Darbi in Balochistan’s Bolan district.

On October 13, four people, including a woman, were killed and five others injured when a van travelling from Quetta to Kalat collided with a truck on the Quetta-Karachi National Highway near Badrang in Mastung district.

stories.title: One dead, another injured as boiler explodes at Karachi chemical factory
summary: One worker died, and another sustained serious burn injuries on Wednesday after a boiler exploded at a chemical factory near Port Qasim in Karachi's Bin Qasim area, police said.

Read: Factory fire brought to heel after eight-hour battle On Monday, a massive fire engulfed and precariously damaged a garments factory near Metroville in Karachi’s SITE area, prompting the deployment of fire and rescue teams.
On September 7, A fire broke out at an old-clothes factory in Karachi’s Landhi Export Processing Zone (EPZ).

stories.title: Bear injures man in Balakot
summary: He said the black bear sneaked into the populated area from the nearby alpine forest that provides a natural habitat for the animal and injured a resident, Taj Mohammad.
Mr Amir said the injured man was shifted to the Tehsil Headquarters Hospital, Balakot, where doctors provided him with medical treatment and rabies vaccine.
The SDO said black bears were attracted to maize crops and often entered agricultural fields in search of food, and when people crossed their paths, the animals could attack and injure them.

stories.title: Sadiq urges Pakistan to fix top order
summary: Pakistan have made a promising start to building a strong combination for the 2027 ODI World Cup, which will be jointly hosted by South Africa, Zimbabwe and Namibia in late 2027.
Under the leadership of Shaheen Shah Afridi, Pakistan have won back-to-back matches against Sri Lanka and England in the ODI tri-series being played on home soil.
Salman Ali Agha scored a century against Sri Lanka, while Hasan Nawaz and young all-rounder Arafat Minhas impressed against England.

stories.title: Medical fraternity condemns ‘harassment’, registration of FIRs against doctors
summary: KARACHI: Medical bodies have strongly condemned the prevailing hostile work environment at health facilities, stating that cases of harassment, violence and the registration of FIRs will force doctors not to take critical cases.

Fully implement healthcare protection acts across all provinces to secure hospitals, emergency wards, and clinical staff from mob violence, political intimidation, and illegal police actions,” he said.

stories.title: 13 measles cases recorded in South Waziristan
summary: SOUTH WAZIRISTAN: Measles cases have been reported in different areas of Lower South Waziristan, raising concerns about the spread of the infectious disease among children.
They urged relevant authorities to improve healthcare services, ensure availability of essential medical facilities at the hospital and provide timely treatment to children suffering from measles.
They asked the health authorities to strengthen vaccination efforts and improve treatment facilities at Wana hospital to protect children from the disease.

stories.title: SC issues notices to KP IG prisons, ACS for not complying with its order
summary: PESHAWAR: The Supreme Court on Tuesday issued show cause notices to the Khyber Pakhtunkhwa inspector general of prisons and the additional chief secretary (home), directing them to appear in person today (Wednesday) to explain their position for not complying with its order.

The bench had subsequently issued notices to the KP advocate general, the inspector general of prisons and the additional chief secretary (home), seeking a joint report containing para-wise comments within a fortnight.

Today, when the case was taken up, neither the Inspector General of Prisons nor the Additional Chief Secretary, Home and Tribal Affairs Department, KPK, are in attendance nor there is any intimation why they could not appear,” the bench observed.

stories.title: Karachi hospital sealed for negligence after infant contracts mpox
summary: KARACHI: The Sindh Healthcare Commission (SHCC) has sealed a private hospital in Malir after receiving a report from the district health officer (DHO) about a laboratory-confirmed mpox case in an infant.

Following the report, SHCC officials, with the support of the DHO Korangi and the SSP, took action and sealed the hospital, which was being run illegally by non-qualified staff and quacks,” said the statement.
Last week, a 40-day-old baby tested positive for mpox and he was under treatment at the Sindh Infectious Diseases Hospital & Research Centre (SIDH&RC).

stories.title: Mine owners seek lifting of explosives ban in KP
summary: PESHAWAR: The Frontier Mine Owners Association has urged the officials of relevant departments to resolve the mining sector’s genuine problems instead of making the provincial minerals department a target of political criticism.

Mr Tanoli said the minerals department had been subjected to politically motivated criticism for several years and had faced hundreds of inquiries and National Accountability Bureau (NAB) cases over the past two decades.
Mr Tanoli said illegal mining remained a serious challenge for the provincial government.

stories.title: Interior ministry asked to report on ‘missing’ TLP leaders by Lahore High Court
summary: Justice Muhammad Jawad Zafar was hearing a petition filed by Sarwat Fatima, a leader of the banned party, challenging the alleged detention of the Rizvi brothers and seeking their recovery.
All the SHOs denied having arrested the Rizvi brothers.
The brothers went ‘missing’ following a police operation against TLP protesters near Muridke on Oct 13, 2025.

stories.title: Hybrid seed can take wheat production to 98 maunds per acre: University of Agriculture Faisalabad VC
summary: A three-year Letter of Intent, signed by the UAF vice chancellor and Guard Agriculture Chief Executive Shahzad Ali Malik, provides for joint research, multi-location field trials, evaluation of breeding material and potential commercialisation of hybrid wheat.
The UAF vice chancellor said his university had been working on hybrid wheat research for around 15 years in collaboration with an Australian university.
Shahzad Ali Malik said it could take another three to four years to bring hybrid wheat to the commercial stage.

stories.title: Civil judge injured after allegedly being attacked by advocate in Rawalpindi
summary: An FIR was registered against the suspect under Section 7 of the Anti-Terrorism Act at the Civil Lines police station.

Police were deployed at the hospital to ensure the security of the judge, police sources said, adding that the injured judge underwent a medico-legal examination and after obtaining its report the FIR was registered.
He was taken into custody from the office of TMA Rawalpindi and shifted to the City Police Station for further investigation.

stories.title: Accused in Laiba suicide case killed by ‘accomplices’ firing’, police claim
summary: According to him, the under-custody accused was killed during firing on a police team in the jurisdiction of Ramna police station.
The under-custody accused was injured in firing of his accomplices, while the police team remained safe due to bulletproof jackets and protective measures, the spokesperson said.

The spokesperson said the accused was nominated in the case of Laiba Ijaz, the student who committed suicide in Ramna police jurisdiction, and search operations were underway for arrest of his other accomplices.
